payload.summary: WorldEntity bounds stable entity IDs and the pending generation-4 repair bounds persistentState depth/nodes/string bytes, but record metadata strings remain unbounded: kind plus origin.worldId, origin.regionId, origin.generator, and origin.recipeKey accept arbitrary non-empty control-free string length.
payload.impact: A domain record can therefore carry arbitrarily large immutable metadata outside the newly bounded persistent-state budget. That leaves a concrete persistence/memory work boundary unbounded in the canonical WorldEntity contract and can also inflate duplicate diagnostics through kind/recipeKey copies.
sourceProof: main@ae83c0ef470eb2e73d99be41fd3561ede30c40e1: checkedNonEmpty only enforces string type, non-empty, and no control characters; WorldEntity.isId separately caps id at 256 bytes
PR #378 exact head 4680b8176c144b99ffeb1754eb94c03e7bfe42c6 retains the same unbounded checkedNonEmpty path while adding explicit persistent-state string-byte budgets
PR #378 tests lock persistent-state byte limits and malformed metadata types but contain no metadata length-bound regression
repository PR/issue search found no existing WorldEntity metadata-length lane or issue
payload.sourceLevelRepro: Construct WorldEntity.new with a canonical <=256-byte id and ordinary empty persistentState, but set kind and/or origin.worldId/origin.regionId/origin.generator/origin.recipeKey to string.rep('x', 1048576). By source inspection these fields pass checkedNonEmpty because they are non-empty and control-free; no execution claim is made.
recommendedClosure: define explicit documented byte maxima for WorldEntity metadata strings rather than relying on producer discipline
apply the same bounds to WorldEntity.new and owned registry records before storage/diagnostic construction
add exact-limit and one-byte-over pure regressions for kind and each origin metadata field
preserve the existing <=256-byte entity-id contract and pending persistent-state budgets
keep failure atomic and avoid caller-controlled formatting/metamethod execution
payload.integrationNote: This is a distinct follow-on boundary found while PR #378 is awaiting trusted-history recovery. Do not broaden or merge around the active generation-4 recovery without normal lane ownership and fresh exact-head review.
